newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel sells Discount Bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel sells Discount Bank stake.

text.p: Israel's offering of Israel Discount Bank shares and warrants was three times oversubscribed and the price closed on Monday at nine percent above the minimum, underwriter IBI Investment said.

The price closed at 170 shekels for a package of five shares, nine Series Two warrants (part of which are exercisable now and the rest in July) and seven Series Three warrants (exercisable in November). The minimum price had been set at 156 shekels.
The government expects to raise 621 million shekels from the sale of a 17 percent stake in Israel's third largest commercial bank.

The government raised 170 million shekels from the public offering and 42 million shekels from an issue to the bank's workers. It expects to raise another 171 million shekels from the warrants exercised in July and 238 million shekels in November.
The offering was held in two parts: to institutional investors last week and to the general public on Monday.
The government received bids worth 500 million shekels, IBI said.
Prior to the offering, the government held a 79 percent stake in Discount.
The offering was to have taken place in February but was delayed after the Securities Authority asked to see more detailed information on the bank's fourth-quarter debt provision.
The government plans to float about 10 percent in Leumi, Israel's second largest bank, in May.
